items.prompt: The fire is thought ___ shortly before ten o'clock.
items.why: The fire started before the claim was made, so use to have + past participle.
Expected looks forward, so the simple infinitive is right. Next month is not earlier.

items.prompt: She is believed ___ for a bank at the moment.
items.why: At the moment means in progress now: to be + -ing.

items.prompt: The painting is reported ___ stolen last night.
items.why: Last night is earlier, and the painting did not steal itself: to have been + past participle.

items.prompt: The two companies are said ___ in talks right now.
items.why: Right now means the same time as the claim: to be.

items.prompt: He is understood ___ the country before the police arrived.
items.why: Before the police arrived is earlier: to have + past participle.

items.prompt: There is thought ___ a gas leak under the street, so the road is closed.
items.why: After is thought use a to-infinitive: there is thought to be.

items.prompt: The minister is said ___ about the plan for years.
items.why: For years looks back from now: to have known.
